images.title: Numbers on both sides of zero
images.purpose: Show that a number line goes on past 0, so there are numbers less than 0.
images.composition: One long horizontal number line centred with wide space above and below it, and two short labels under it.
images.exact_structure: One horizontal grey #6B7280 line with an arrowhead at each end and 7 equally spaced ticks, marked from left to right −3, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3. The tick for 0 has a reddish purple #CC79A7 dot. A teal #0072B2 bracket under the 3 ticks right of 0 and an amber #E69F00 bracket under the 3 ticks left of 0. Exactly 7 ticks, 1 line, 2 brackets.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any extra floor, dot, arrow or row beyond the counts stated
unequal floor rows or unequal arrow lengths
images.takeaway: There are numbers less than 0, on the left of 0.
images.description: A horizontal number line with 7 equal ticks from −3 to 3; 0 is marked with a purple dot, the 3 ticks to its left are bracketed amber and the 3 to its right teal.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at 0 and then at a place on the line that is less than 0.

image_decisions.why: A number line makes numbers less than 0 visible in one clean picture.
